text:
olivia-privacy: Heads up — received a DSAR from an EU user earlier today. They want full deletion of account data + embeddings + any attachments. Legal asked for proof of deletion and a manifest of what was removed. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRIV-2890 :eyes:

emma-legal: Thanks olivia. They supplied requester verification. Can we confirm whether there are any active retention holds? I think there was a vulnerability triage last week that might have preserved relevant artifacts.

keith-sec: Correct — during the vuln triage we put a temporary forensic hold on related project buckets (project-id: customer-demo-42). That hold is in our internal tracker but not in the DSAR manifest. We need to reconcile.

mike-ops: Quick tech question: some attachments are stored as S3 objects encrypted with KMS key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01. The key was rotated yesterday; snapshots exist from before rotation. If we delete objects and remove snapshots, can we still produce crypto-proof that objects were deleted?

sanjay-infra: Short answer: rotation alone doesn't make past ciphertext undecipherable. Old ciphertext remains decryptable by the current key material unless keys are scheduled for deletion or disabled. The problem is if we need to preserve data for forensic analysis while also complying with erasure — legal conflict.

emma-legal: So we need a retention-exception if forensic keeps data. We can't ignore the DSAR. Options: 1) grant a narrow exception with explicit scope & TTL, 2) ask user to consent to temporary hold, or 3) redact and delete non-forensic bits. Preferences?

natalie-ml: Also important: embeddings store may have vectors derived from the user's content. Our embedded-index retention/erasure flow currently does async deletion. That could leave ephemeral query-side caches for a bit. We need to ensure chain-of-custody proof for embeddings too.

keith-sec: Proposal: create a minimal retention-exception ticket that documents: reason (ongoing vuln triage), scope (exact paths + S3 prefixes + embedding ids), owner (sec/forensics), TTL (7 days), and audit requirements (who accessed, when). Capture it in PRIV-2890 and send notice to user with redacted justification per GDPR guidance.

olivia-privacy: Legal is ok with a short, narrow exception if we can provide the proof and a manifest at the end. They asked we avoid broad indefinite holds.

mike-ops: Implementation notes: we'll need a small RBAC change — create a timebound role `forensic_read_temp` scoped to the project bucket and attachments prefix. It must be auditable (no service-account access; human accounts only) and expire automatically. I can implement via Terraform + IAM condition.

sanjay-infra: I'll prepare KMS check: ensure key isn't scheduled for deletion and backup snapshots are accounted for. If any snapshot is stored offsite or in long-term backup, we must list it in the exception. Also verify encryption context used for embeddings (we use customer-id in context).

keith-sec: Add audit logging steps: enable object-level access logs for the prefixes, ensure CloudTrail entries are preserved (separate retention) and capture all accesses to the `forensic_read_temp` role. We'll append log hashes to the final manifest as proof of handling.

emma-legal: For user-facing communications: provide a deletion manifest showing what was removed and what was retained under exception, with clear TTL and contact for appeal. Legal will draft template.

natalie-ml: For embeddings: mark the vectors with an `erasure_hold` flag in index metadata so deletion workers skip them until exception clears. That way we can guarantee no queries hit them by using query-time filters, while still keeping them available for forensics.

olivia-privacy: Sounds good. Can we also capture requester verification and chain-of-custody steps in the PRIV ticket? We should avoid separate docs.

mike-ops: Action items I can take: 1) terraform PR for timebound role, 2) enable object-level logging for the prefixes, 3) coordinate KMS snapshot inventory. ETA: 4 hours for PR + 2 hours for logs + inventory timeframe depends on KMS check.

sanjay-infra: I'll run `aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef01` and `aws s3api list-object-versions` to enumerate snapshots/versions and post results. If any object uses a deleted key, we have to escalate.

keith-sec: I'll draft retention-exception form and add the minimal fields. I'll also note the automatic TTL revoke and require a secondary approval from CISO for extension beyond 7 days.

emma-legal: Legal will prepare the user notice and the deletion manifest template. We'll need sec/infra to provide the manifest content (paths, object versions, embedding ids) plus cryptographic log hashes.

olivia-privacy: Great. Please post updates here. Also tag me if you need escalation to privacy counsel.

sec-bot: Incident bot: PRIV-2890 created and linked. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRIV-2890

mike-ops: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4823 — terraform role `forensic_read_temp` with expiry condition. PTAL @sanjay-infra @keith-sec

sanjay-infra: KMS inventory: no scheduled deletions, one old snapshot in glacier-backup-bucket (versionId: v-20240201). Flagged it in PRIV-2890 under artifacts needing explicit listing.

keith-sec: Retention-exception drafted and attached to PRIV-2890. Scope is bucket prefixes `customer-demo-42/*`, S3 versions [v-20240201], embedding ids [embed:cus-42-*], TTL 7 days. CISO notified for approval.

emma-legal: Approved by Legal on condition TTL is enforced and access logs are provided at close. I'll prepare the user notice after we compile manifest.

olivia-privacy: Thanks all. After TTL expiry, runbook step: 1) delete embeddings (async job), 2) remove S3 versions, 3) rotate any ephemeral keys if used, 4) produce final manifest and send to user. Make sure final message includes hash of manifest and log bundle.

mike-ops: Will do. I'll post verification logs and manifest hash in PRIV-2890 when complete.

keith-sec: Closing note: if forensics discovers additional related artifacts, we MUST reopen exception and notify Legal & Privacy. No unilateral extension.

olivia-privacy: Acknowledged. Thanks everyone :folded_hands:
